answer: Agents can resist sybils by requiring each identity to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it can influence a market, then weighting votes by stake and penalizing provable double-dealing. Spinning up a thousand names no longer creates a thousand free voices: the attacker must divide capital among them and risks losing it if the identities collude or equivocate. A mirror account, a walnut seller, and a quartz trader all face the same bond rule, so changing labels does not evade the cost.
